newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 30.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Australian Securities Commission has requisitioned a report prepared for engineering group Australian National Industries by Robert Ellicott, QC, over ANI's 1991 purchase of German waste company ABT from Kerry Packer, and is seeking independent legal dvice over any action it should take after ANI withdrew from legal action. The Australian Stock Exchange is also expected to react later this week. Page 1.

Hong Kong-based airline Cathay Pacific is set to sell its A$210 million Australian data processing centre, which was enticed to Australia by a Federal Government incentive five years ago. The centre's operations are also expected to be outsourced to another company. Page 1.

Retailer Woolworths Ltd and wine maker Mildara Blass Ltd have expressed interest in purchasing parts of mail-order and telemarketing services group Cellarmasters, after Cellarmasters managing director Terry Davis announced the group is considering a A$100 million float and will make a decision soon. Page 19.

As speculation intensifies over the future of grocery retailers and wholesalers Davids Ltd, the group is expected to announce today changes to senior management, as well as the sale of some non-retail assets and possible asset writedowns. Page 19.

Malcolm Turnbull, the lawyer who became well known for his involvement in the Spycatcher case and shocked the finance sector when he tried to take over Russia's Sukhoi Log gold mine, was yesterday appointed managing director and chairman of Goldman Sachs Australia and New Zealand, a process that will absorb his own investment bank into Goldman. Page 19.

After being told by rivals Foxtel and Australis Media Ltd the proposed single programming joint venture will not proceed, Optus Communications intends to strongly oppose the merger between the two companies. The joint venture would have brought the three companies together, but would have given them freedom to retail separate programming packages. Page 20.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Market observers are expecting a A$860 million takeover bid for Joseph Gutnick's Great Central Mines by North American mining heavyweight Barrick Gold as early as today. It is understood Barrick will make a full cash bid of A$3.40 a share for Great Central, which is Australia's sixth largest gold producer. Page 21.

The Australian Securities Commission has used its compulsory powers to obtain a copy of a report prepared for Australian National Industries on the 1991 deal involving ANI's purchase of a European waste management company from Kerry Packer's Consolidated Press Holdings. The ASC is taking action on the deal after ANI pulled out of planned legal action yesterday. Page 21.

Despite its refusal to release information on damning allegations raised by the Colorado Gaming Control Commission, poker machine company Aristocrat Leisure Industries will resume trading tomorrow. Aristocrat said the information would not be released until it is in a position to "adequately respond to those allegations." Page 21.

BHP Copper plans to cut US$22 million in costs from its Robinson copper mine in the United States state of Nevada, but will not cut into the workforce. The plans to cut costs follow a performance review of BHP's North American assets acquired through the A$3.2 billion takeover of Magma Copper. Page 23.

Australis Media shares rose 13 per cent yesterday after a 24-hour halt on trading on the back of positive investor sentiment for the proposed merger between Australis and Foxtel. The increase comes despite reports the merger will need "significant additional capital" to reach positive cash flow. Page 23.

The Becker Group yesterday acquired Dendy cinema and distribution group for less than A$5 million. The purchase will draw Becker into the film exhibition business through Dendy's four cinemas in Sydney and two in Brisbane, yet Becker intends only to concentrate on the distribution business, not the cinema chain. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian National Industries directors decided yesterday the costs of taking legal action against Kerry Packer's Consolidated Press Holdings over the 1991 purchase of German company ABT would not justify embarking on "uncertain and protracted litigation. However, the Australian Securities Commission may decide to take legal action over the deal. Page 25.

In its June quarter production report released yesterday, Plutonic Resources suggested it could make large writedowns on the value of its gold assets in its annual results, and said continuing rumours that central banks around the world were considering further sell-offs of gold reserves were responsible for gold's recent poor performances. Page 25.

Australia's infrastructure sector boomed in the 12 months to June as two infrastructure funds listed on the stock exchange and two airports and three power stations were sold, mainly to banks, local shareholders and foreign buyers. However, the boom has left victims, such as the Hills Motorway Group, Envestra, Chase Manhattan and the Macquarie Bank. Page 25.

Malcolm Turnbull and his business partner, former New South Wales Premier Neville Wran, will this Friday take up positions with Wall St powerhouse Goldman Sachs. Turnbull has been appointed managing director of Goldman Sachs Australia and New Zealand, an Wran will become a senior adviser. Page 25.

MMI managing director Pieter Franzen said yesterday the company is considering a possible entry into the life insurance market and will, as part of cost-cutting, be restructuring its administrative operations. Franzen said MMI wished to move into other insurance lines outside its present operations of general insurance and workers' compensation. Page 27.

The A$4 billion Westfield Trust yesterday reported sales growth of 2.3 per cent for the six months to the end of June, and Stephen Lowy, the managing director of Westfield's Australian operations, said the group expected better results for the second half Page 27.
THE AGE

Australian National Industries yesterday abandoned a possible lawsuit over its 1991 purchase of German waste-to-energy business ABT from Kerry Packer's Consolidated Press Holdings. As ANI directors decided instead that it was in the shareholders' interests to concentrate on the company's future, the Australian Securities Commission may take legal action over the deal. Page B1.

Malcolm Bligh Turnbull will close down his boutique merchant bank Turnbull & Partners to join famous Wall St investment bank Goldman Sachs as chairman and managing director of the Australian and New Zealand operations. Turnbull's business partner, former New South Wales Premier Neville Wran, will also join Goldman as a "senior adviser". Page B1.

In a move that will push its business further towards film distribution, listed film and television group Becker yesterday purchased the independent Dendy Cinemas and Distribution for an undisclosed sum. Becker is expecting distribution, which was once asmall part of the business, to reap in more than 40 per cent of the company's earnings. Page B2.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics estimates in its annual report that half of the net growth in this decade's recovery of Australia's capital stock is investment in housing, while mining and a few service industries take up most of the rest. Page B3.

Politicians, local authority representatives, Trades Hall officials and members of the textile, clothing and footwear industry will rally against Industry Commission recommendations for large cuts in tariffs to the TCF industry. The rally coincides with he beginning of Melbourne hearings on the IC's draft report on the future of the TCF sector. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
